## What it solves

### Remote control

> help, approval cards, per-bot memory, remote screen, voice calls and "needs you / done" notifications — the same features, without being tied to one model or one subscription.

### Mobile access

> > **Why the iPhone app can be a version behind:** every iPhone release goes through Apple's App Review first, which usually takes a day or more, so the App Store version can trail the Mac, Windows, Linux and host releas…

### Multi-agent orchestration

> other visible bots and message one; the reply comes back to it as a new turn, and it answers you then.

### Agent runtime

> Codync turns the coding agents on your computer — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, OpenCode, Grok Build, Gemini, Copilot, Hermes Agent and ~40 more — into persistent *bots* you delegate to from your iPhone, Mac, Windows…

### MCP support

> in its own session, and can react to each other, up to 3 rounds.

### Security & isolation

> ut being tied to one model or one subscription.

### GUI / desktop app

> OS, Windows and Linux (static on Linux, runs on any distro) that drives every agent, keeps the transcripts and serves every client.

### Notifications

> 40 more — into persistent *bots* you delegate to from your iPhone, Mac, Windows PC, Linux desktop or any terminal, the way you'd message a colleague.

### Cross-agent support

> Mentions Amp, Claude Code, Codex, Copilot
